title: Transplant status and rejection
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's transplant status or transplant complication only.
note:
Chief Complaint
Routine follow-up for status post heart-lung transplant.

HPI
The patient is a 38-year-old woman who presents for a routine follow-up clinic visit. She underwent a heart-lung transplant several years ago. She reports feeling well today and denies any new symptoms, shortness of breath, or chest pain. She states that she feels stable on her current immunosuppressive regimen and has not experienced any issues since her surgery. She continues to manage her daily activities without significant limitations and reports good exercise tolerance. She denies any fever, chills, or malaise.

Review of Systems
The patient reports no constitutional symptoms, no respiratory distress, and no cardiac complaints. She denies any neurological deficits, musculoskeletal pain, or gastrointestinal upset.

Social History
The patient works full-time as an administrative assistant and lives with her spouse and a dog. She reports a non-smoking status and drinks alcohol socially on weekends.

Family History
Mother has hypertension. Father has type 2 diabetes. Siblings are healthy.

Medication List
Tacrolimus 2mg twice daily
Mycophenolate mofetil 500mg twice daily
Prednisone 5mg daily
Lisinopril 10mg daily

Vitals
Temperature: 98.6 F
Blood Pressure: 118/76 mmHg
Heart Rate: 72 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Oxygen Saturation: 98% on room air
Weight: 155 lbs

Recent Labs
Tacrolimus trough level: 8.5 ng/mL
Hemoglobin: 13.2 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 6.4 x 10^9/L
Platelet Count: 210 x 10^3/uL
Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL
eGFR: 85 mL/min/1.73m2

Exam
General: The patient is alert and oriented x3. She appears well-nourished and in no acute distress.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. S1 and S2 are normal. No murmurs, rubs, or gallops noted.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezes, rales, or rhonchi.
Integumentary: Skin is warm and dry with no signs of rashes or lesions.

Assessment
The patient is a 38-year-old woman who remains stable following her heart-lung transplant. She is currently asymptomatic and demonstrates excellent tolerance of her medication regimen. Lab work remains within expected parameters for a post-transplant patient.

Plan
1. Continue current immunosuppressive medications as prescribed.
2. Monitor tacrolimus trough levels every 3-6 months.
3. Routine lab work to be repeated in 3 months.
4. Patient instructed to contact the clinic immediately if she develops a fever or any new respiratory symptoms.

Electronically signed, D. Kowalski, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Heart and lungs transplant status: one code, Z94.3, which maps to two HCCs (221 and 276).

distractors.why: Both heart and lungs were transplanted: Z94.3.
